title: arXiv Trending AI — Wednesday, 4 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred ordering relies mainly on Hugging Face Papers votes, a narrow platform-attention signal, and citation evidence is limited for same-day papers.

sections.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
sections.abstract: The authors develop a framework and broad benchmark suite for routing among specialized models and policies, reporting that learned routing can improve quality-cost trade-offs across language, vision, generation, coding, and robotics tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper's abstract reports an omni-modal trajectory matrix covering 25 benchmarks and 374,401 scored runs, and learned routers that reduce policy time while improving results on selected modalities.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state in Appendix D that their theory assumes a fixed state distribution, so it does not cover states dependent on the router's earlier choices; they also note the complexity of step-level routing for long-horizon agents.

sections.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
sections.abstract: LoCo identifies states where a reasoning model appears to have enough information, trains on shorter verified continuations preferred at those states, and reports reduced token use with maintained or improved accuracy on math and code benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract and evaluation section describe state-conditioned DPO preference pairs built from self-generated traces; they report 41.7–45.4% shorter math completions and 23.4–36.3% shorter code completions while maintaining or improving accuracy on their tested suites.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported training uses a single 7B base model and math-only generated training traces; results on eight math/code benchmarks do not establish transfer across model families or to other task domains.

sections.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
sections.abstract: The Kling team presents a technical report on how multimodal understanding, captioning, reference grounding, prompt enhancement, reward modeling, and evaluation interact in controllable audiovisual generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' report argues that generation quality depends on the full data–conditioning–alignment–evaluation chain and describes a system-specific design and evaluation stack for controllable video generation.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a technical report centered on the authors' Kling systems and pipeline; its observations are not an independent, controlled comparison of competing video-generation systems.

sections.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
sections.abstract: DreamX extracts compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion model's spatiotemporal features to separate action dynamics from appearance, with the authors reporting transfer across embodiments and environments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract says DreamX compresses each latent video frame from 1,200 to 4 tokens and reports state-of-the-art results among latent-action models on LARY-Bench, plus zero-shot transfer tests.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's comparative result is tied to LARY-Bench and the reported transfer tests; it does not establish performance in real-world robot deployment.

sections.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
sections.abstract: FactEmbed uses factorized latent representations to model the visual change expressed by a reference image and modification text before forming embeddings for composed-image retrieval.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract describes factor-level contrastive learning plus distillation into a deeper attention layer, and reports better performance than prior work across composed-image-retrieval benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The claims concern composed image retrieval; the abstract does not establish that the representation improves general multimodal reasoning outside this task family.

sections.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
sections.abstract: ToolSpace mines tool dependencies from execution traces to synthesize replayable, state-aware environments and multi-step tasks for training and evaluating long-horizon tool-using agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract reports harder AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking variants and improvements for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and GLM-5.2 across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation is based on synthesized environments and named benchmark suites derived from available service traces; performance on unseen real-world service workflows remains to be established.

sections.title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
sections.abstract: YANAMI provides 400,000 multimodal dialogue examples and a 400-dialogue benchmark for testing whether models can maintain and visually realize changing interaction state across turns.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract reports that fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves image editing, generation, and stateful-interaction scores, while the benchmark reveals remaining state-tracking and visual-realization failures in current unified multimodal models.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's fine-tuning result is for BAGEL; it does not show that the same gains transfer to other model families or training setups.

sections.title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
sections.abstract: VidUEU-Agent iteratively curates instruction data from raw video and packages 100,000 examples into a dataset for multimodal understanding, editing, and unified tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' abstract describes a four-stage video-to-instruction pipeline that updates the data distribution using downstream training results and reports gains across representative benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not name the benchmarks or quantify effect sizes, so the size and reproducibility of the reported gains cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
